<description>
When a reorg lowers the tip, `removeForReorg` can evict BIP68 transactions that are still valid at the new tip, together with all their descendants.

A transaction that spends an unconfirmed parent gets its lockpoints cached with that input at height tip+1. After `invalidateblock`, `TestLockPointValidity` can still pass on those cached lockpoints (always when every input was unconfirmed, since `maxInputBlock` is then genesis; and with mixed confirmed and unconfirmed inputs when the confirmed input's block survives), so `CheckSequenceLocksAtTip` is evaluated against stale values and the transaction is removed.

The fix, suggested by ismaelsadeeq, is to never evict on cached lockpoints alone: if they are not valid at the new tip, or the cached sequence-lock check fails, recalculate them with `CalculateLockPointsAtTip` and evict only if the fresh result also fails. This covers height-based and time-based locks alike, at the cost of some recalculations that turn out to be unnecessary.

test_reorg_stale_lockpoints() in feature_bip68_sequence.py covers four cases across a reorg: a BIP68-disabled child, a BIP68-enabled child of an unconfirmed parent, a child with mixed confirmed and unconfirmed inputs, and a time-based zero lock where the reorg lowers the median time past (test by Bicaru20). The test fails on master, and the mixed-input case also fails on the earlier genesis-only version of this fix.

test_reorg_unsatisfied_lock_evicted() (by instagibbs) is the counterpart: it checks that transactions whose relative lock is genuinely unsatisfied after the reorg are still evicted, together with their descendants.

Reproducer for unpatched nodes:
https://gist.github.com/javierpmateos/c55d365973adbf488a852dc5e0b77dec

Same class of issue fixed for TRUC in #33504.

Closes #35007
</description>

+    # Counterpart to test_reorg_stale_lockpoints(): a transaction whose relative
+    # lock is genuinely unsatisfied at the new tip must still be evicted, with its
+    # descendants, even though its cached lockpoints stay valid (the block of its
+    # confirmed input survives the reorg).
+    def test_reorg_unsatisfied_lock_evicted(self):
+        node = self.nodes[0]
+        relative_height = 3
+
+        funding_locked = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, confirmed_only=True)
+        funding_mixed = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, confirmed_only=True)
+        funding_parent = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, confirmed_only=True)
+        self.generate(node, 1, sync_fun=self.no_op)
+        # The block after these is the first one that satisfies the relative lock.
+        blocks = self.generate(node, relative_height - 1, sync_fun=self.no_op)
+
+        locked = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, utxo_to_spend=funding_locked["new_utxo"], sequence=relative_height)
+        locked_child = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, utxo_to_spend=locked["new_utxo"])
+        # Mixed inputs: the same lock on a confirmed input, a zero lock on an unconfirmed one.
+        parent = self.wallet.send_self_transfer(from_node=node, utxo_to_spend=funding_parent["new_utxo"])
+        mixed = self.wallet.create_self_transfer_multi(
+            utxos_to_spend=[funding_mixed["new_utxo"], parent["new_utxo"]],
+            sequence=[relative_height, 0],
+        )
+        node.sendrawtransaction(mixed["hex"])
+        mempool = node.getrawmempool()
+        for tx in (locked, locked_child, parent, mixed):
+            assert tx["txid"] in mempool
+
+        # One block back: the funding block stays in the chain, so the cached
+        # lockpoints remain valid, but the next block no longer satisfies the locks.
+        node.invalidateblock(blocks[-1])
+        mempool = node.getrawmempool()
+        assert locked["txid"] not in mempool
+        assert locked_child["txid"] not in mempool
+        assert mixed["txid"] not in mempool
+        assert parent["txid"] in mempool
+
+        node.reconsiderblock(blocks[-1])
+        self.sync_blocks()
+        self.wallet.rescan_utxos()
+
     # Use self.nodes[1] to test that version 2 transactions are standard.
     def test_version2_relay(self):
         mini_wallet = MiniWallet(self.nodes[1])

[2026-11-04] rc:4472073348 inline on src/validation.cpp by instagibbs (member) (edited 2026-11-04):
This stuff is janky enough, and the above comment stale enough, that we should consider being a bit more explicit about what's happening. Putting assumed invariant here makes it more clear? @ismaelsadeeq

```
        const LockPoints& lp = it->GetLockPoints();
        // Fast path: the cached lockpoints still refer to blocks in the active chain and let the
        // tx into the next block, so keep it.
        // A failure here is not conclusive. Inputs that were unconfirmed when the tx entered the
        // mempool were assumed to confirm at the old tip + 1 (at the old tip's median time past),
        // which is too strict once the tip has moved back. Recompute the lockpoints against the
        // new tip and decide on those. (A cached pass needs no recheck: unconfirmed inputs can
        // only have zero relative locks, which recomputed lockpoints always satisfy.)
        const bool cached_lock_points_pass{TestLockPointValidity(m_chain, lp) && CheckSequenceLocksAtTip(m_chain.Tip(), lp)};
        if (!cached_lock_points_pass) {
            const CCoinsViewMemPool view_mempool{&CoinsTip(), *m_mempool};
            const std::optional<LockPoints> new_lock_points{CalculateLockPointsAtTip(m_chain.Tip(), view_mempool, tx)};
            // Evict only if the tx can't go in the next block with its recomputed lockpoints.
            if (!new_lock_points || !CheckSequenceLocksAtTip(m_chain.Tip(), *new_lock_points)) return true;
            it->UpdateLockPoints(*new_lock_points);
        }
```
